facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
the mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies and neurologic examination were unremarkable
a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone without adjacent soft-tissue swelling
a lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables, and an associated soft-tissue component
a lobulated frontal-bone mass measuring 3.7 × 3.3 × 2.8 cm
was hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences

concepts.why: The patient's painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, well-circumscribed and soft, is consistent with an osteoma, a type of benign bone tumor.
The lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction, as well as the avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences, are characteristic of a giant cell tumor.

The presence of a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction, along with the patient's unremarkable laboratory studies, could suggest a brown tumor, a type of bone lesion associated with hyperparathyroidism.

The lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction, as well as the avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences, are also consistent with an aneurysmal bone cyst, a type of benign bone lesion.
The presence of a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and cortical destruction could also suggest fibrous dysplasia, a type of bone disorder that can cause lesions and deformities.
